risks.description: Wave 3 contains two tasks (post-approval-summary and bounded-repair) that both depend on human-approval-gate but are intended to be mutually exclusive based on gate outcome. If the gate approves, only post-approval-summary should run; if it rejects, only bounded-repair should run. The decomposition does not explicitly encode this conditional fork—it relies on the orchestrator to implement conditional execution logic. If the orchestrator runs both tasks or neither, the pipeline produces incorrect results.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the orchestrator supports conditional task execution based on gate decision output. Explicitly configure Wave 3 so that post-approval-summary runs only on approval and bounded-repair runs only on rejection. Add explicit branch points to the decomposition if the orchestrator requires them.

risks.description: Wave 0 tasks (process-set-a, process-set-b, validate-workflow-spec) assume that evidence/set-a.json, evidence/set-b.json, and CLAUDE.md exist and are readable in the working directory. If any of these files are missing or inaccessible, Wave 0 tasks will fail immediately with no fallback or recovery.
risks.mitigation: Before DAG execution, verify that all three input files (evidence/set-a.json, evidence/set-b.json, CLAUDE.md) exist in the working directory and are readable. If any are missing, halt DAG execution and ask the user to provide them.

risks.description: The bounded-repair task description states 'if the gate rejects or validation fails,' but does not clarify whether 'validation fails' refers to failures in Wave 0 tasks (process-set-a, process-set-b, validate-workflow-spec) or only to synthesis validation. If it refers to Wave 0 failures, repair is impossible because bounded-repair runs after the gate (Wave 3), which is downstream of Wave 0. This ambiguity may cause the assigned skill to misunderstand the task scope and timing.
risks.mitigation: Clarify the bounded-repair task description: if it only handles synthesis-level feedback, remove the 'or validation fails' clause and explicitly state it runs post-gate on synthesis rejection. If it is meant to repair Wave 0 failures, restructure the DAG to include a repair task in Wave 1 (after Wave 0, before synthesis) with a bounded-retry loop.

risks.description: The DAG will write output files (findings-a.json, findings-b.json, and implied synthesis.json). If files with these names already exist in the working directory with valuable data, they will be silently overwritten.
risks.mitigation: Before Wave 0 execution, check for existing findings-a.json, findings-b.json, and synthesis.json files. If any exist, warn the user and optionally offer to back them up or ask for confirmation before proceeding.
